headline: Recommended revised Pressed Cafe signage and Granite Group signs, and voted to invite Cummings Center to discuss its sign variance.
summary: The board reviewed two sign applications, recommending changes to a Pressed Cafe sign proposal and approving a sign and awning plan for The Granite Group with one exception. It also discussed the Cummings Center's global sign variance history and voted to invite a company representative to a future meeting, and heard an update on proposed revisions to the city's Sign Ordinance.
decisions: Recommended that the first floor Pressed Café sign be revised to include the bean drop logo centered in the sign band, that the 'coffee, juice, panini, pizza, catering' sign be moved to the right side, and that the second floor Pressed Café sign be removed from the application, 6-0.
Recommended approval of the signs for The Granite Group, 97 River Street, subject to submitted plans, except for internal illumination of the awning sign, 6-0.
Voted to invite a representative of the Cummings Center to the Board's next meeting to discuss the global sign variance, 6-0.
Approved the May 7, 2026, meeting minutes as amended, 6-0.

2. Discussion regarding the status of the Global Sign Variance at 181 Elliott Street, Beverly, 62 
MA 10915, The Cummings Center 63 
 64 
Clawson stated that it appears after 2012, the Cummings Center stopped coming before the ZBA 65 
or the Board itself or would flip flop between the two. The Cummings Center received its first 66 
variance in 1998 which allowed for nine wall signs in 11 locations, no colors, and up to 80 wall 67 
signs on the first floor of the entire complex. New buildings have been added to the property 68 
since that time, but the locations for signs on the second floor and above were specifically 69 
identified and do not include the 500 and 200 buildings. In 2004, the variance was changed to 70 
allow red and blue colors on the signs on the second floor and above. There are existing signs on 71 
the building that have various colors. These received individual variances. In 2009, the number 72 
of second story and above signs was increased to 11 signs total in 16 locations. There are 73 
currently 33 signs.  74

Hutchings stated that the only leverage to get the Cummings Center to come back and amend the 76 
variance is to withhold recommendations for new sign requests. There is no place where the 77 
existing clutter impacts the public way. The clutter is contained to the buildings themselves. 78 
Clawson stated that the closest thing to clutter would be the front of the 900 buildings. The 79 
variance should be updated to show where all the existing signs are and where new signs will be 80 
allowed. Barone Jr. stated that the terms and conditions of the variance have been surpassed and 81

3. Update on the progress of the proposed revisions to the City of Beverly Sign Ordinance 91 
 92 
Erin Schaeffer, Economic Development Planner, stated that she has been working on the Sign 93 
Ordinance for about two years. The Sign Ordinance was so far out of date that it needed to be 94 
started from scratch. The goals are for the Sign Ordinance to reflect the most updated case law, 95 
to streamline the permitting process and make it easier for businesses to obtain signage, and to 96 
allow for creativity and emerging technologies. From the enforcement side of things, there was 97 
not previously a lot of clarity regarding how to measure signs. She has researched ordinances 98 
from various communities and then spoken with businesses regarding their experiences. Some 99 
items of importance are clarifying standards and definitions for each sign type, the number of 100 
signs allowed by each business depending on the circumstances and defined by sign type, and 101 
expanding and clarifying sign illumination standards and considering new sign technology. She 102 
created a new sign table by sign type and zoning district. Many of the signs are by-right and this 103 
streamlines the process for businesses. She is working on a provision for businesses to want a 104 
wall sign, a window sign, and a projecting sign for pedestrians to be able to see them.  105 
 106 
Schaeffer stated that there are some items that come before the Board that likely do not have to, 107 
such as changes of sign copies. Signs should come before the Board if they are freestanding or 108 
monument signs, as the siting of these can be complicated. Changeable message signs should 109 
also come before the Board. She would like to speak with the Board more about a potential 110 
electronic messaging sign at the Cummings Center, as one has been requested for some time. 111 
Other electronic signs are currently allowed in theaters over 50 seats. She stated that she is 112 
considering that the Board could be given jurisdiction of historic signs in Town, in consultation 113 
with the Historic Districts Commission. There was a suggestion that the Board work as an 114 
advisory board for signs that may need to go for a variance or special permit. 115 
 116 
Barone Jr. asked about adding enforcement into the Sign Ordinance. Hutchings stated that this 117 
has been considered before but determined not to be reasonable or viable.  118
